subject: Clarify: penetration-test coverage & remediation timeline for Hosted / Dedicated / VPC / On‑prem
body:
--- Message 1/6 ---
From: Lydia Chen <security@acme-corp.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Pen test coverage question + remediation ETA

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for sending over the draft SIG and the pen-test PDF we received last week. Our security team flagged an item that references a "privilege escalation vector" discovered during the assessment. Before we loop this into procurement, we need clarity on two things:

1) Which deployment types were included in that pen-test? Specifically: Hosted API (multi-tenant), Redwood Dedicated (reserved single-tenant pools), Private (Redwood control plane with customer VPC), and on‑prem/air‑gapped packages.
2) For any findings that affect Hosted, what remediation steps have you completed and what remains open? We need a timeline and any evidence we can attach to our vendor risk assessment.

Can you confirm scope and next steps by EOD Thursday?

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Chen
Security Program Manager, Acme Corp
---

--- Message 2/6 ---
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question + remediation ETA

Hi Lydia — thanks for the note and sorry for the initial ambiguity.

Short answer up front: the referenced penetration test report covers our Hosted runtime and Dedicated (Redwood-managed) pools. Private/VPC deployments were partially in scope (control plane interactions only) — fully customer-managed on‑prem packages were out of scope for that engagement. Im putting Monica (security) and Sergio (AE on your account) on this thread for the technical breakdown and evidence.

I attached a quick scope matrix and an initial remediation tracker that maps findings to deployment types. Well follow up with a formal attestation and the supporting artifact links.

Attachments: redwood_pt_scope_matrix_v1.xlsx (scope matrix), remediation_tracker_dec2026.xlsx (tracker)

Next step: Monica will call out which findings apply to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC and list whats fixed vs in progress. Expect that in a separate email within the day.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3/6 ---
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Lydia Chen <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question + remediation ETA

Hi all — Monica from Security. Below is the explicit breakdown of scope from the December 2026 pen test (engagement ID: PT-2026-11-01) and the current remediation status. Ive included which findings are applicable to each deployment type and links to the artifacts we can provide.

Summary of scope (what the engagement covered):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed, multi-tenant control plane + shared inference runtime): Full dynamic assessment, internal and external network testing, privilege escalation and container isolation checks.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed single-tenant GPU pools): Same runtime vector testing as Hosted where Redwood controls the GPU fleet and orchestration (findings that touch the runtime apply here).
- Private/VPC (Redwood control plane + customer-managed VPC network peering): Control plane components, API auth flows, and documented networking interfaces were tested. Note: customers VPC-resident hosts were not attacked directly; we validated control plane interactions and egress boundaries.
- On‑prem / air‑gapped: Out of scope for this engagement unless a customer engaged on-site services.

Key finding referenced by Acme: "Privilege escalation via container runtime misconfiguration"
- Affects: Hosted (YES), Dedicated pools where Redwood manages the orchestration (YES), Private/VPC (Only control plane pieces; the customers hosts are not tested)
- Root cause: A combination of outdated container runtime kernel modules and an overly-permissive mount configuration in a legacy autoscaling helper service used in Hosted pools.

Remediation status (high-level):
- Hosted: Mitigated (Completed 2026-12-05) — actions: kernel modules updated across all multi-tenant inference hosts; autoscaling helper service reconfigured to drop unnecessary mounts; runtime sandbox tightened (seccomp profile enforced); privilege escalation paths validated with regression tests. Evidence: [attachment: redwood_pt_report_hosted_v1.pdf], audit logs and rollout manifest (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-evidence).
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): Mitigated (Completed 2026-12-06) on Redwood-managed pools; customers with pinned/legacy orchestration will receive guidance for remediation steps (we provide the fix script and a checklist).
- Private/VPC: Not vulnerable in the customers VPC host context (we did not execute intrusive tests inside customer VPC). However, control plane APIs that interact with customer resources had a low-severity finding around token scoping — we rotated service tokens and added stricter scoping rules (Completed 2026-12-08).
- On‑prem: N/A (out of scope) — we provide a recommended hardening checklist for customers running our on‑prem package; if Acme expects us to include on‑prem scans we can schedule a separate engagement.

Planned evidence deliverables we can provide to Acme this week:
- Signed remediation summary PDF (attestation) for Hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated (will include CVE references and timestamps).
- Full pen-test PDF redacted for customer-sensitive test vectors [attachment: redwood_pt_report_hosted_v1.pdf].
- Remediation tracker with verification status and regression test results [attachment: remediation_tracker_dec2026.xlsx].
- Optional: short recording of the remediation validation run (internal Red Team exec/demo).

Open items and ETA:
- Formal signed attestation: 2026-12-18 EOD (Monica)
- Evidence bundle (redacted pen-test + audit manifests): 2026-12-18 EOD
- Additional on‑prem scoping call (if requested): propose week of 2026-12-27

If you need an explicit table mapping "finding -> deployment types -> evidence link" for Procurement, I can paste that inline or attach as CSV.

Monica Patel
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

--- Message 4/6 ---
From: Lydia Chen <security@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question + remediation ETA

Thanks, Monica — that breakdown helps. Two follow-ups:
1) Procurement will want a machine-readable matrix (CSV) that shows, per finding, the deployment types impacted and remediation status (fixed/in-progress/not-applicable). Can you attach that?
2) Our security reviewers also asked for timestamps and the person who validated the remediation for Hosted (need name + date + validation artifact).

Also — would Redwood be willing to provide a short attestation PDF saying: "Findings affecting Redwood-hosted runtime have been remediated as of DATE, validated by Redwood Security" with an authorized signature? That will speed our vendor approval.

Best,
Lydia

Subject: Re: Pen test coverage question + remediation ETA

Karthik Iyer

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Two last asks before we close the vendor review:
- Please include the signed attestation PDF in the Drive folder and share the link to the specific artifact (Procurement likes a direct file URL).
- If possible, can Redwood run one short verification by your Red Team (non-invasive smoke) and share the short runbook/video clip showing the validation? Thats not mandatory but would expedite our internal approval.

If you can get the attestation and the direct artifact link by EOD today well push this through.

Thanks — Lydia
